articles.title: Rivales ingleses compiten por Matias Fernandez Bardo | YSscores
articles.excerpt: Arsenal, Liverpool y Newcastle compiten por fichar a Matias Fernandez Bardo.
articles.content:
Arsenal y Liverpool han entrado en competencia con Newcastle para asegurar la firma de Matias Fernandez Pardo, el jugador del Lille, en los últimos días de la ventana de transferencias de verano.

El jugador tiene 21 años y puede jugar como extremo izquierdo o delantero. Participó en 41 partidos la temporada pasada, anotando 8 goles y proporcionando 7 asistencias.

El Telegraph informó que Newcastle está intensificando sus movimientos para adquirir al internacional belga, que el Lille ha valorado en 60 millones de libras. Mientras tanto, TEAMtalk indicó que el Liverpool se ha puesto en contacto con el club francés, habiendo identificado al jugador como un reemplazo para Ismaïla Sarr.

Según "CaughtOffside", Arsenal ha entrado en la carrera y ha realizado consultas sobre el traspaso, indicando que el club podría cambiar su atención a un movimiento formal después de resolver la situación con Julián Álvarez.

Bardo ha llamado la atención de Mikel Arteta, especialmente por su capacidad para jugar en varias posiciones de ataque. Sin embargo, las demandas financieras del Lille representan un obstáculo para el traspaso.

El interés del Arsenal en el jugador surge después de que el traspaso de Julian Alvarez se haya complicado, con David Ornstein afirmando que las posibilidades de que el delantero del Atlético de Madrid se mueva al club londinense parecen escasas, dado el deseo del jugador de unirse al Barcelona.

David Ornstein ha indicado que el Atlético de Madrid está preparado para negociar con el Arsenal sobre el traspaso de Julian Alvarez. Sin embargo, Alvarez ha informado a Arteta que no está interesado en hacer el cambio, aunque su postura podría cambiar antes de que cierre el mercado de fichajes.

articles.title: Officer killed, another injured in Columbia shooting; SLED investigating
articles.excerpt: SLED is investigating an officer-involved shooting near a park on Hazelwood Road that took the life of an officer and injured another.
articles.content:
COLUMBIA, S.C. (WIS) - The South Carolina Law Enforcement Division (SLED) is investigating an officer-involved shooting near a park on Hazelwood Road Saturday morning that took the life of an officer and injured another.

According to police, the shooting resulted in the death of 29-year-old Chris DeLong. DeLong was hired by the department in 2024 and graduated from the Criminal Justice Academy in January 2025, when he was assigned to the Southeast region.

“Our hearts are broken this evening,” Columbia Police Chief Skip Holbrook said. “We gather under the worst circumstances you could possibly imagine.”

Another officer, David Dymock, was injured in the shooting and has since been released from the hospital.

“We are grateful to share that Officer David Dymock’s condition has improved, and he has been released from the hospital,” the department said in a statement.

“As Officer Dymock continues his recovery and recuperation at home, we ask that you continue to keep him and his family in your prayers. The road to recovery continues, and we know the support surrounding him will mean so much in the days ahead.

CPD extends our appreciation to everyone who has reached out, offered assistance, shared words of encouragement, made donations, and continued to keep both of our officers and their families in your prayers."

Police say the suspect, 33-year-old Adam Dowdy of Prosperity, was also killed in the shooting.

The incident began when officers received a call around 9:27 a.m. from a woman reporting a domestic dispute in the 100 block of Holstein Lane.

After DeLong arrived around 9:43 a.m., the woman told police that she had a restraining order against Dowdy, and learned he had already left the residence. The complainant provided DeLong with Dowdy’s name, a physical description, and a vehicle description.

Minutes later, DeLong initiated a call at 951 Hazelwood Road regarding a suspicious person standing near a vehicle that matched the description.

Police say Dymock responded to that call as backup.

Around 10:45 a.m., Dymock radioed other law enforcement officers to report that shots had been fired and Dowdy was down. Police later confirmed that Dowdy was the same suspect from the incident on Holstein Lane.

According to Chief Holbrook, Dowdy had several prior arrests across multiple states, including South Carolina, Kentucky, Wisconsin, and Georgia.

“Pray for the DeLong family to have strength as they navigate this unimaginable time,” Chief Holbrook said during a press conference. “Pray for Officer Dymock’s recovery, pray for his family, and pray for these police officers that serve so courageously in our capital city.”

CPD says the South Carolina Law Enforcement Division (SLED) and the Richland County Sheriff’s Department are assisting with the investigation.

articles.title: Heavy Metal Band on Their Last Legs as Another Band Member Abruptly Quits
articles.excerpt: Guitarist AJ Rebollo of Bad Wolves explained the ugly music industry reasons that made him finally leave the band.
articles.content:
Bad Wolves is one of the most chaotic bands we’ve had in a long time. Take a look at their Wikipedia, and you’ll immediately get a headache from the amount of turnaround. Vocalists, guitarists, and bassists all have come and gone, to the point that the band is barely the same anymore.

Now, we can add another name to the list of people leaving the band for good. In a lengthy post on Instagram, guitarist AJ Rebollo revealed that he’ll be stepping away from the band for the foreseeable future. Thankfully, it’s a little different than your typical band drama. He argued that the Bad Wolves were being handicapped by the band.

Videos by VICE

“In short, I can no longer in good faith remain a member and co-sign the decisions constantly being made FOR this band by the label,” Rebollo wrote. “Among other issues I have with the inner workings of this business.”

The moment the guitarist knew he had to leave actually centered around the death of Dolly Parton. According to AJ Rebollo, the label decided to green light a Dolly Parton cover they had in the vaults. The group themselves decided against dropping the record because they wanted to work with Parton personally on the record. Apparently, the label had other ideas.

Bad Wolves Lose Another Member of Their Band

“We, as an entity, told the label we had no interest in releasing the cover after learning of Dolly’s unfortunate passing, as her collaboration on the song was no longer a possibility. We felt it would (understandably) be interpreted as somewhat of a capitalization on her passing from an outside perspective. They went ahead and posted that we were releasing it anyway, despite efforts from more than one member, myself included, to oppose it,” Rebollo continued.

All of these funky music industry woes led the Bad Wolves guitarist to grow increasingly disenchanted with the business. Consequently, he found it vital to preserve the love he has for music by leaving the band. Fear and all, he stressed that keeping that was the most important.

“Music is my job, my livelihood, and most importantly, my passion,” Rebollo said. “Stepping away from this is absolutely terrifying as I am sacrificing what little I have left when it comes to stability within the music world. I do not know what the future holds for me regarding that… I loved creating this upcoming album with [Bad Wolves] as I think it is a genuinely incredible piece of art, but this is a decision I just have to make.”
